title: fix(sessions): show recovery guidance for tombstoned room sessions
body:
Refs #146276

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

This is a same-repository branch; GitHub's fork-only maintainer-edit toggle does not apply.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users mentioning an agent after restart recovery exhausted its attempts received no response explaining how to recover. Admission rejected the tombstoned session before reply generation; Buzz only logged the propagated exception.

Reported by @chachi-max (#146276).

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared reply dispatcher sends a recovery reminder through the normal channel reply path while preserving the original admission rejection. A bounded, process-local cache suppresses repeated attempts for the same session and recovery cycle; reset, deletion, or Gateway restart clears suppression. Every visible admission rejection logs the session key, tombstone reason, and recovery hint at warn level.

The notice also works in message-tool reply mode. Explicit send-policy denial, private ACP delivery, and non-user events retain their existing restrictions. Model-locked sessions point to WebChat's **Resume in new session** instead of an unavailable reset.

There are no new configuration options, schema changes, or durable recovery records. Automatic replacement remains an open persistence-design decision. No CLI cleanup behavior or command family changes.

## User Impact

A session tombstoned by restart recovery now tells the room once how to recover instead of silently dropping messages. An authorized `/reset` or `/new` starts a fresh context while preserving the existing transcript; later ordinary inbound can be admitted again.

Suppression retains at most 1,024 session entries. An evicted entry or a new Gateway lifetime can produce another reminder. Notification delivery failures preserve the original rejection; the warning log remains available.

## Evidence

The new regression failed before the fix at the channel deliverer assertion: `Number of calls: 0`, after admission returned the expected restart-recovery error. After the fix, the notice suite passes: first inbound reaches the channel deliverer, second inbound adds no notice, and each rejection reaches the main warn sink. It also covers reset/delete invalidation, model-lock guidance, message-tool mode, and explicit suppression policies.

Validation:

- Focused admission/reset/dispatch run: **33 passed**, including real `/new` and `/reset`, retained transcript, and subsequent ordinary admission and initialization.
- Final notice suite after review fixes: **14 passed**. Added cases first reproduced late ACP ownership, late send-policy denial, ambiguous routed delivery, and absent dispatcher receipts, then passed after repairing the checks.
- Full restart-recovery suite: **202 passed**.
- Buzz inbound suite: **36 passed**.
- Existing CLI lifecycle and Buzz target/thread tests: **43 passed**; these do not reproduce the reported deletion failure.

```sh
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.artifacts/vitest-fs/l189-final node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.restart-tombstone.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/reply-turn-admission.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.delivery.test.ts -t 'tombstone|recovery guidance'
OPENCLAW_VITEST_FS_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=.artifacts/vitest-fs/l189-review-fixes node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.restart-tombstone.test.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery.test.ts extensions/buzz/src/inbound.test.ts
```

The required `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` gate passed. Final core and messaging-test typechecks, targeted lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed after the review fixes. Independent Codex autoreview is scoped-clean through P2, with no accepted/actionable findings. Review findings about current delivery restrictions and uncertain receipts were reproduced and resolved.

CI is **green** on `f08b930c6f343d510626015652f0caa09b5999e7`: [CI run 34714257990](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34714257990). The repository watcher completed with `GREEN` and zero pending checks on that exact head.

### Known gaps and follow-up

The reported CLI UUID failure was not reproduced. Current `sessions delete` first calls `sessions.list`, then forwards the selected key to the same Gateway deletion owner used by direct RPC. The standard Buzz UUID peer shape is accepted by the inspected parser. Existing CLI forwarding and Buzz target/thread parsing tests passed; they are not end-to-end proof of the reporter's failed deletion. RPC `dryRun` rejection is intentional; the CLI preview uses `sessions.list`.

@chachi-max: please share a redacted stack trace for the failing `openclaw sessions delete` command, the exact OpenClaw version, and whether `openclaw sessions list --agent <id> --json` also fails. Preserve the key's structure while replacing private identifiers consistently. This will distinguish list preflight from deletion cleanup before changing either owner.

No live Buzz relay or published-updater proof was run. This change handles channel feedback after admission rejection; it does not change update execution or persistent recovery behavior.


## ClawSweeper review

ClawSweeper reviewed `f08b930c6f343d510626015652f0caa09b5999e7` and found no actionable defects; no code fixups were needed. The suggested Telegram Test Server proof is deferred under the maintainer's landing decision: this repair has dispatcher-boundary proof, and no live Telegram or Buzz validation is claimed. Automatic replacement and the unreproduced CLI deletion problem remain follow-ups under #146276.
